title: House Robber
statement: You are given a list `nums` of house values. You cannot rob two adjacent houses. Return the maximum amount you can rob.

predict_steps.prompt: For house i, the two choices are rob it (then skip i-1) or skip it. Which recurrence?

viva.question: Why does House Robber use a choose-or-skip DP in linear time?
expected_points: each house decides between skipping or taking with the best before the previous house
adjacent houses cannot both be taken
each index is processed once so time is linear
the recurrence stores the best total up to that house

viva.question: What breaks on a one-house array if you still look two steps back?
expected_points: the only choice is to take that house
there is no adjacency conflict yet
base cases must cover length one before the main loop
reading dp[i-2] blindly would go out of range

viva.question: Why is skipping the previous house sometimes better?
expected_points: taking house i-1 blocks taking house i
the recurrence keeps the max of skip versus take
a smaller previous take can unlock a larger current take
local choices accumulate into the global optimum via optimal substructure
